problems.title: A sine addition formula
problems.question: Solve sinxcos2x+cosxsin2x=1.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The left side issin3x.
steps: Thus3x=π/2+2πk, so x=π/6+2πk/3, for any integerk.

problems.title: Equal sine and cosine squares
problems.question: Solve sin²x=cos²x.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: cos2x=cos²x−sin²x=0.
steps: Thus2x=π/2+kπ, orx=π/4+kπ/2. This is equivalent tox=±π/4+kπ.

problems.title: First two positive sine roots
problems.question: Find the sum of the two least positive roots ofsinx=1/2.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The first roots are π/6 and 5π/6.
steps: Their sum is π.

problems.title: Diagonal sections of a rhombus-based pyramid
problems.question: A pyramid has rhombus base with acute angle 60° and four equal apothems. Find the ratio of its diagonal-section areas.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Equal apothems place the height foot at the rhombus centre. Both diagonal sections therefore have the same height.
steps: Their areas are proportional to the base diagonals. For a 60° rhombus, those diagonals are √3a and a.
The larger/smaller section ratio is √3.

problems.title: Dihedral angle of a regular hexagonal pyramid
problems.question: The lateral-edge/base-edge ratio is 13:10. Find the dihedral angle at the base.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Scale the base edge to 10 and lateral edge13. The base apothem is 5√3; the face apothem is √(13²−5²)=12.
steps: In the perpendicular section, the cosine of the dihedral angle is base apothem/face apothem=5√3/12.

problems.title: A half-angle substitution
problems.question: Find the least positive root ofcos(x/2)=1+cosx.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Putt=cos(x/2); then1+cosx=2t².
steps: Solvet=2t², so t=0 or 1/2. The least positive correspondingx is 2π/3; the t=0 branch first gives π.

problems.title: A linear system in tangent and cosine
problems.question: Solve tanx/√3+2cosy=2,√3tanx−2cosy=2.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Adding gives(4/√3)tanx=4, so tanx=√3.
steps: Substitution gives 2cosy=1. Thereforex=π/3+kπ and y=±π/3+2pπ, with integersk, p.

problems.title: Apply tangent to an arctangent equation
problems.question: Solve arctan((x−1)/3)=π/3.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The principal arctangent is inverted by tangent on(−π/2,π/2).

problems.title: A section through two symmetric edge midpoints
problems.question: In a regular square pyramid, a plane passes through midpoints of SB, SC and an interior base point. What property must its section have?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The midpoint segment is parallel to BC. The plane’s base trace is also parallel to BC.
steps: The section is a trapezoid. Reflection in the pyramid’s central plane perpendicular to BC preserves the cutting plane and interchanges its two legs.
Thus the trapezoid is isosceles, and every isosceles trapezoid is cyclic.

problems.title: Two different face apothems
problems.question: A pyramid has height 1 over the centre of a parallelogram with sides 6,3 and corresponding heights2,4. Find lateral are a.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The centre-to-side distances are 1 for the length-6 sides and 2 for the length-3 sides. Face apothems are √2 and √5.
steps: The two length-6 faces together have are a 6√2, and the two length-3 faces together3√5.
Total lateral are a=6√2+3√5.

problems.title: Keep the domain of a later expression
problems.question: A root of 1+sin2x=sinx+cosx is substituted into tanx+cotx. Which listed value can result?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Puts=sinx+cosx. The equation iss²=s, so s=0 or 1.
steps: Ifs=0, then sinxcosx=(s²−1)/2=−1/2 and tanx+cotx=1/(sinxcosx)=−2.
Ifs=1, the product is 0, so the requested tangent-cotangent sum is undefined and cannot be used.

problems.title: One sine root family contains the other
problems.question: Solve sinx·sin3x=0.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: sinx=0 givesx=kπ; sin3x=0 givesx=kπ/3.
steps: The first family is contained in the second. The full solution is x=kπ/3.

problems.title: Amplitude determines whether a sine-cosine equation is solvable
problems.question: Which listeda makes(a−1)sinx+(a+1)cosx=4 solvable?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The amplitude is √[(a−1)²+(a+1)²]=√(2a²+2). Require this to be at least4.
steps: Thusa²≥7. Among1,−√3,2,−√5,√6,−2√2, only −2√2 qualifies.

problems.title: Normal of a plane through three cube-edge midpoints
problems.question: Find cosine of the angle between the base of a cube and the plane through midpoints of AB, AD, CC₁.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Use a unit cube. The points are(1/2,0,0),(0,1/2,0),(1,1,1/2), with plane x+y−3z=1/2.
steps: Its normal is(1,1,−3); the base normal is(0,0,1). The absolute normal-dot cosine is 3/√11.

problems.title: Face angle versus a large diagonal-section angle
problems.question: A regular hexagonal frustum has acute lateral-face angleα and acute largest diagonal-section angleβ. Which relation holds?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Let the base-edge difference beΔ and lateral edge L. Then cosα=(Δ/2)/L.
steps: The largest diagonal-section base lengths are twice the hexagon sides, so their difference is 2Δ andcosβ=Δ/L.
Thereforecosβ=2cosα.

problems.title: A sum of squares vanishes term by term
problems.question: Solve(cos(x+y)−1)²+sin²(x−y)=0.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Both nonnegative terms must vanish: x+y=2πk, x−y=πp.
steps: Adding and subtracting givesx=πk+πp/2, y=πk−πp/2, for integersk, p.

problems.title: Split an absolute sine equation by its sign
problems.question: How many roots has|sinx|=sinx+2cosx on[0,2π]?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: When sinx≥0, the equation requirescosx=0; when sinx<0, it requiressinx+cosx=0.
steps: The first branch givesx=π/2. The second givesx=7π/4 in the lower half-plane. Endpoints0,2π fail.
There are 2 roots.

problems.title: Double the angle of a principal arccosine
problems.question: Evaluate sin(2arccos(1/3)).
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Forθ=arccos(1/3), cosθ=1/3 andsinθ=√(1−1/9)=2√2/3.
steps: Thensin2θ=2sinθcosθ=4√2/9.

problems.title: How many equal edges can a pyramid have?
problems.question: What is the maximum edge count of a nondegenerate pyramid whose every edge is equal?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: An equal-sided convex base with all vertices equidistant from the apex is regular. For basen-gon sidea, its circumradius is a/[2sin(π/n)].
steps: Positive pyramid height requires the lateral edgea to exceed that radius, so sin(π/n)>1/2. Hence n<6.
The largest possible base has 5 sides, so the pyramid has 5 base plus5 lateral edges,10.

problems.title: Circumsphere of a tetrahedron’s edge midpoints
problems.question: A regular tetrahedron has edge6. Find the common distance from the point equidistant from all six edge midpoints.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The six midpoints for m a regular octahedron centred at the tetrahedron centre. Their radius is a/(2√2).
steps: Witha=6, the radius is 3/√2=3√2/2. The three opposite midpoint pairs make this centre unique.

problems.title: Add two principal arctangents
problems.question: Evaluate arctan(1/3)+arctan(1/4).
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The tangent of the sum is(1/3+1/4)/(1−1/12)=7/11.
steps: Both angles are positive and their sum is belowπ/2, so it is the principalarctan(7/11).

problems.title: Compare complete trigonometric solution sets
problems.question: Four answers are Mary:π/4+kπ/2; George:±π/4+kπ; Tamar:(−1)^kπ/4+kπ; David:π/4+kπ. Exactly two are correct. Who is wrong?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Mary and George describe the same set:all odd multiples of π/4.
steps: Tamar gives only π/4,3π/4 modulo2π; David only π/4,5π/4 modulo2π. Their sets differ from each other and from Mary’s.
The only equal pair is Mary/George, so they must be the correct pair. Tamar and David are wrong.

problems.title: One cosine level in each of two quadrants
problems.question: For whicha does2cos²x−(2a+3)cosx+3a=0 have exactly one root in each of(0,π/2),(3π/2,2π)?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: The polynomial factors as(2cosx−3)(cosx−a). The first factor cannot vanish for realx.
steps: On each of the two stated intervals, cosx takes every value in(0,1) exactly once.
Thus the condition is 0<a<1.

problems.title: Two intersecting altitudes imply perpendicular opposite edges
problems.question: In tetrahedron ABCD, the altitudes from D to ABC and from B to ACD intersect. Which opposite edges must be perpendicular?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: AC is perpendicular to each of those two altitude lines, since it lies in both corresponding face planes.
steps: The intersecting altitude lines span a plane containing B, D. A line perpendicular to both is perpendicular to that plane.
HenceAC is perpendicular to BD.

problems.title: A frustum with equal base-sum and lateral area
problems.question: In a regular triangular frustum, the base dihedral angle isα and the base-are a sum equals lateral are a. Find smaller/larger base-are a ratio.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard trigonometric equation or a right-triangle spatial model.
formulas: Let base sidesa>b. Slant apothem=√3(a−b)/(6cosα), so lateral are a=√3(a²−b²)/(4cosα).
steps: Equate this to √3(a²+b²)/4. Then(a²−b²)/(a²+b²)=cosα.
Thus(b/a)²=(1−cosα)/(1+cosα)=tan²(α/2).
